summary: Mt. Hood NF lookout: 1924 first cabin, present 41-ft R-6 tower from 1973, staffed in summers, destroyed by the Grasshopper Fire, reported August 1, 2026.

facts.design: R-6 flat cab on a 41-foot timber tower (1973); earlier 30-foot L-4 pole tower (1932) and 40-foot pole tower with 6 by 6 foot cab (1924)
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Mt. Hood National Forest (Barlow Ranger District)
facts.status_note: Destroyed by the Grasshopper Fire, reported August 1, 2026. No source describes what remains on the summit.

access.note: Fire closures apply. The Forest asks visitors to observe all closures and fire restrictions. The sources do not say whether the summit is inside a closure.

visit.trail_note: The lookout burned in 2026, so there is no structure to visit. Before the fire, summer access was by road (4WD or AWD recommended on the recreation.gov listing) and winter access was on skis, snowmobile or snowshoes.

events.note: First lookout: a 6 by 6 foot cab on a 40-foot pole tower
Replaced with an L-4 cab on a 30-foot pole tower
Present R-6 flat-top cab on a 41-foot timber tower
Lightning-caused Grasshopper Fire spotted east of Grasshopper Point on July 23
Destroyed by the Grasshopper Fire. The Forest said 'last night' in its August 1 release; another report says the early morning hours of Saturday, August 1

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 41 feet per NHLR, firelookout.com and cherylhill.net. 40 feet per recreation.gov and Your Oregon News. Story says most sources give 41 feet and notes the dissent. Record height is 12.5 m (41 feet); the brief's 12.2 m equals 40 feet.

The Forest's August 1 release says the lookout was destroyed 'last night'; Your Oregon News says the early morning hours of Saturday, August 1. The story says overnight into August 1 and gives both accounts.
The NHLR page predates the fire and still reads as a standing lookout. Status comes from the 2026 Forest Service release and news reports.

notes_for_editor: Rental: the brief's rental.available false is consistent with the fire, but recreation.gov still lists the lookout as a place to stay, so the listing needs fixing. The brief's 2004 'restored' event (repainted, steps repaired by the chapter) could not be verified: the NHLR visit reports show only a 2007 visit, and the FFLA 2004 PDF returned no readable text. It is left out; please check the PDF or drop the event. OregonLive (the story said 'century-old') returned 403 and is not used. Brief elevation 1717.9 m is consistent with NHLR's 1,718 m.
